solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Only part of the circle gets the stories and secrets

parts.note: an arc is a section of a circle's circumference
ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person

explanation.surface: Someone hears only a fragment of a gossiping circle's tales and secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a gathering of anecdotes, is an old crossword favourite; the two parts are simply set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are mysteries or hidden knowledge known only to initiates, matching the plural noun secrets.

clue.text: Rough walk over Aussie territory

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over something means sitting above it, so the walk comes first

parts.note: a stride is a long step, a way of walking
NT is Australia's Northern Territory

explanation.surface: A hard trek across the Australian outback.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or noise is harsh and grating, which is one sense of rough.

clue.text: Erect French huts that look out of place in London station

indicators.note: things out of place are wrongly arranged, so the letters must be put in a new order

parts.note: the three words supply all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone puts up incongruous French-style huts at a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenchurch Street is a mainline railway terminus in the City of London, serving Essex commuter lines.

clue.text: Sugary woman left at home

parts.note: a woman's name
standard abbreviation for left
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A sweet-natured woman stays behind in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully sentimental, and sugary describes cloying sentimentality in the same way.

clue.text: One of two with new status after the match

definitions.text: One of two with new status after the match

parts.words: One of two with new status after the match
parts.note: surface reading: a player in a doubles pairing whose ranking changes after a sporting fixture
setter's reading: the match is a wedding, after which each of the couple is now a spouse

explanation.walkthrough: Match suggests a game, but here it is a marriage match; the two are the newlyweds, each with a fresh legal status.
explanation.definitionFit: Each half of a newly wed couple is a spouse, whose status changes from single once the union is made.

clue.text: Goin' on two wheels over one island

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over, that is above, the second

parts.note: cycling, with the final G dropped as the apostrophe in Goin’ signals
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone cycles across a small island.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Goin’ tells you to clip the G from the cycling word too.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll is a Pacific island in the Marshall Islands, famous for nuclear tests.

clue.text: Violent person, a jerk hard inside

indicators.note: the hard element sits inside the jerk, wrapped by its letters

parts.note: a tug is a sudden pull
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A violent man is described as a hard-hearted jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a brutal ruffian who uses force, so a violent person fits as a noun.

clue.text: It's good? Nonsense!

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the claim that something is good.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue dismisses something as worthless, which is what this slang word means.
explanation.definitionFit: Grot is British slang for junk or rubbish, the sort of thing anyone would scornfully deny is any good.

clue.text: Woman of 27 heading west

indicators.note: an across answer read heading west runs right to left, backwards

parts.note: the answer to 27 across, a greeting

explanation.surface: A woman from a certain place travels westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to another entry in the grid, the Latin greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva is a female given name, so it stands for a woman as crosswords commonly allow.

clue.text: A carefree land

parts.note: taken as written
light-hearted, without worries

explanation.surface: A happy-go-lucky country.
explanation.walkthrough: Land looks like a noun, a country, but it is the verb meaning to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to descend and settle, as a bird or passenger comes to rest, which is to land.

clue.text: Fellow in charge without love, starchy type

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the charge letters surround the love

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A stiff, prim man has been put in charge but lacks warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: Without seems to mean lacking, but here it means outside; starchy type looks like a stuffy person but is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc, also called cassava, is a tropical root crop rich in starch, used for tapioca.

clue.text: Wendy's family favourites

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the household of Wendy in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Wendy's family members are her favourite people.
explanation.walkthrough: In J M Barrie's Peter Pan, Wendy, John and Michael belong to the Darling family.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname plural names Barrie's family, and the common noun means dearly loved people, both fitting the plural.

clue.text: 'Invalids' with a nature that's perverse?

indicators.note: something perverse is contrary and twisted, so the letters are turned into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People who think themselves ill have a contrary disposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes hypochondriacs, quote marks suggesting their illness is self-proclaimed, while the same words supply all the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Valetudinarians are people anxiously obsessed with their own health, often imagining they are sickly, hence so-called invalids.

clue.text: No one will be listened to, sister!

indicators.note: being listened to means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: no one is none, said out loud

explanation.surface: A cry to a sister that nobody is going to pay her any attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman in a religious order, addressed as Sister, so sister is a fair title for her.

clue.text: Communication shows agreement's not right

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: a contract is a formal agreement
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A message reveals that a deal is not correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact means being in touch, an exchange of messages, so it is a form of communication.

clue.text: Dismissed? Yell — there's no place for silence!

indicators.note: no place for means the quiet word is left out

parts.note: to shout is to yell
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A batsman given out yells in protest where quiet is expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Dismissed is the cricket sense: a batsman who is dismissed is out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a dismissed batsman is out, so the adjective and past participle swap cleanly.

clue.text: What's rustic is nice, except for the lake

indicators.note: except for means the lake letter is excluded

parts.note: pleasant means nice
L abbreviates lake

explanation.surface: The countryside is lovely apart from the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic as a noun is a country person, an unsophisticated rural dweller, the same as a peasant.

clue.text: Posted with enclosed money to serve as deposit

indicators.note: enclosed means the money is held inside the posted word

parts.note: posted a letter means sent it
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Cash is mailed off as a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Deposit looks like money paid in advance, fitting the surface, but means matter settled at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is material that settles out of a liquid, which a geologist or chemist calls a deposit.

clue.text: In a church losing a hundred of the old people

indicators.note: losing means the hundred is taken away

parts.note: belonging to the Church of England
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A congregation in a church dwindles by a hundred elderly members.
explanation.walkthrough: The old people are the Angles, the Germanic tribe that settled East Anglia; old people suggests elderly churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglian is the adjective relating to the Angles, an ancient Germanic tribe, so it means belonging to that people.

clue.text: Huge number in MI6, not half a dozen!

indicators.note: not means the half dozen is removed from the total

parts.note: read as numbers: Roman M and I, then 6
half of twelve

explanation.surface: An enormous headcount at the spy agency, fewer than six.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence service, but read as numerals it is M (a thousand), I (one) and 6; drop the six.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, as in the Arabian Nights title, is idiomatic for a vast or countless quantity.

clue.text: Drug one took in after operation

indicators.note: after means the eating word follows the earlier pieces

parts.note: op is short for operation
Roman numeral one
took in food means ate

explanation.surface: A patient was given a painkiller following surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium, such as morphine, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Right-winger with one atrocious trick

indicators.note: atrocious means dreadful, so the word is badly mangled into new order

parts.note: taken as written
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A conservative politician pulls one dreadful stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A neocon is a neoconservative, someone on the political right favouring assertive foreign policy.

clue.text: Local bigwig almost genuine, not a rodent

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the bigwig is cut
not a means the article's letter is taken away from genuine

parts.note: the squire is the chief landowner in an English village
genuine means real
taken as written

explanation.surface: A village grandee is nearly authentic, yet is no rat.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a rodent reads as a denial; but not only removes the article, and rodent is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel is a bushy-tailed tree-dwelling animal of the order Rodentia, hence a rodent.

clue.text: Group heading off for court

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the group is dropped

parts.note: a squad is a group or team

explanation.surface: A team sets off for the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A quad, short for quadrangle, is an enclosed courtyard in a college, which is a court.

clue.text: Drum that introduces a nursery rhyme

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall narrow drum beaten with the hands
second meaning: the opening words of ..., the Piper's Son

explanation.surface: A drumbeat opens a children's song.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme begins Tom, Tom, the Piper's Son, stole a pig and away he run.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a percussion instrument and the first two words of a well-known children's verse.

clue.text: Covering with which chap binds a set of books

indicators.note: binds means wraps round, as a cover holds pages

parts.note: a chap is a male
NT is the New Testament, a set of biblical books

explanation.surface: A man uses a cover to bind a series of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a cloak or any enveloping layer, so it is a covering.

clue.text: Greeting a famous victory

parts.note: taken as written
VE Day, Victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Hailing a celebrated triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: VE stands for Victory in Europe, marked on 8 May 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is the Latin word of salutation, hail, used as a greeting or farewell.

clue.text: New Age light source

parts.note: N abbreviates new
an eon is a vast age

explanation.surface: A fresh spiritual movement sheds illumination.
explanation.walkthrough: New Age suggests the alternative spiritual movement, but the words split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon gas glows when electrified and fills advertising tubes, so it is a source of light.
